summary: One content-egress policy for every path that sends session-derived text off this container. Both implementations (config/hooks/lib/egress-policy.cjs and services/nostr-pod-bridge/src/egress_policy.rs) MUST agree with this table and with tests/fixtures/egress-redaction.v1.json.

paths.content: Selected turn text: lifecycle lines, the user prompt, and the last assistant text. Never the whole transcript.
paths.recipients: A NIP-59 gift-wrapped self-DM to the derived mirror child key by default, or one explicit operator pubkey (legacy). Recipients must be 64-char lowercase hex and must appear in the non-empty AGENTBOX_MIRROR_RECIPIENTS allowlist.
paths.providers: None. The body goes to a relay, not to a model provider.
paths.encryption: NIP-59 gift wrap (kind 1059). Encryption is NOT redaction: the body is redacted before it is wrapped.
paths.transport: One relay: NOSTR_MIRROR_RELAY, else the cloud default. NOSTR_RELAYS is deliberately not fanned out.
paths.log_retention: Dry-run previously wrote the composed body to stderr. Under this policy the dry run prints the REDACTED body only, so diagnostics can never retain more than the wire does.

paths.content: Flattened, trimmed user/assistant transcript text sent to a summarisation provider; then a curated digest (summary, actions, questions) published as kind 30840.
paths.recipients: The signed kind-30840 is published to the configured relay and dual-written to the Solid pod. It is NOT gift-wrapped; recipient visibility is the relay/read policy, which is a separate boundary.
paths.providers: The configured summarisation endpoint (ZAI_URL, default the Z.AI API; commonly redirected to the LAN Ontology Loom). This is the only path that hands session text to a model provider.
paths.encryption: None on the provider hop beyond TLS; the published digest is signed, not encrypted.
paths.transport: Provider HTTP request, then relay publish and pod write.
paths.log_retention: Diagnostics name sizes and outcomes, never bodies.

switches.AGENTBOX_EGRESS: Global. '0' disables EVERY path in this table, whatever the per-path switch says. This is the single off switch the review found missing — AGENTBOX_LIVE_MIRROR=0 was never proof that the separately configured Rust digest path was off.
switches.AGENTBOX_MIRROR_RECIPIENTS: Required comma-separated allowlist of 64-hex live-mirror recipient pubkeys. Missing, empty, malformed or non-matching lists refuse the path before content is read, including dry-run.
switches.AGENTBOX_EGRESS_REDACTION: '0' disables redaction. Refused: the policy treats a disabled redactor as a disabled path, so the egress is SKIPPED rather than sent unredacted.

invariants: REDACT BEFORE EGRESS. Every path redacts the exact bytes it is about to send, before wrapping, before signing, and before any provider request. Encryption, gift-wrapping and curation are not redaction.
A path that cannot redact does not send. Redaction failure is a SKIP, never a fallback to sending the raw text.
Recipients are validated as 64-char lowercase hex against a mandatory non-empty allowlist for the live-mirror path.
Outcomes are reported with the vocabulary below so 'nothing happened' is distinguishable from 'it failed' and from 'it was delivered'.

outcomes.skipped: The path decided not to send. Nothing left the process. Carries a reason.
outcomes.attempted: Bytes were handed to a transport or provider; delivery is not confirmed.
outcomes.accepted: The peer positively acknowledged (relay OK / provider 2xx).
outcomes.failed: The attempt was made and the transport or peer rejected or errored.

notes: Exit code zero from either path means the calling session was not blocked. It is NOT proof of delivery and NOT proof the path was disabled — read the outcome, not the exit code.

register.title: Prompt egress register
register.scope: One row per route by which a prompt, code, a secret-adjacent string or a key can leave the container. The register catalogues routes; the same file's `paths` is the redaction contract for the two routes that implement it. A route with no gate or no accepted-egress record carries a marker. The register records the gap and does not invent a gate or a record.

marker_vocabulary.no-gate: Nothing turns the route off short of removing a credential or a binary.
marker_vocabulary.no-accepted-record: No ADR or dated owner decision accepts what leaves on this route.

register.credential_class: Provider credentials stay devuser-class in this step (owner disposition Q8, 2026-10-03, pending owner review). Each row names the credential it uses.
